name: ember-burn
title: Ember Burn
description: The outgoing frame is set on fire: a noisy burn front eats the bright parts first, the edge boils and glows, charred rims fall away and sparks drift off carrying the frame's colour, uncovering the next scene. Runs its WebGL shader over two built-in panels (a stat and a bar chart, then a render queue; text and colours from variables), not over the host's scenes: 60 frames of the first panel, a 40-frame transition, then the second panel. To use it between your own scenes, copy the shader into your composition and feed it your two frames as textures.
useWhen: A scene change should feel cinematic and physical: the frame is destroyed rather than blended away.
The moment can afford well over a second; the burn is meant to be watched.
The outgoing scene has real content worth consuming: the fire takes the bright parts first.
avoidWhen: The cut has to be quick: a burn compressed under 24 frames reads as a smear; use zoom-blur.
The scenes are cool-toned or clinical and a warm flare would fight the palette: use grain-dissolve.
author: Remocn

variables.label: Label
variables.description: Small caption above the number in the sample scene.

variables.label: Value
variables.description: The big number in the sample scene.

variables.label: Bars
variables.description: Bar heights as percentages, separated by commas (up to 12); the last bar is highlighted.

variables.label: Title
variables.description: Small heading above the list in the sample scene.

variables.label: Rows
variables.description: Rows of the list as name | status, separated by semicolons (up to 5).
variables.default: intro-scene.mp4 | Done; feature-tour.mp4 | Rendering; pricing-outro.mp4 | Queued

variables.label: Patches
variables.description: Size of the burn patches; higher is finer.

variables.label: Content bias
variables.description: How much bright parts burn before dark ones.

variables.label: Resolution
variables.description: Share of the frame size the shader is drawn at, then scaled up. Smoke and flame are soft; sparks are single cells, so 0.75 is the floor.
